ledger.note: 1807: Napoleon creates the Duchy of Warsaw from the Polish lands taken from Prussia. 'It initially comprised the ethnically Polish lands ceded to France by Prussia under the terms of the Treaties of Tilsit' (infobox: 'Treaties of Tilsit: 7 and 9 July 1807'; 'Constitution: 22 July 1807'); initial area 'around 104,000 square kilometres'. The page names the provinces, not a boundary: the region is Cliopatria's 1809 outline.

ledger.note: July 1807: the duchy is a French satellite from its creation. Infobox Status: 'Satellite state of the French Empire, Personal union with the Kingdom of Saxony'; text: 'was a French client state established by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1807' and 'formally an independent duchy, allied to France'; 'never allowed to develop as a truly independent state'. Mirror of first-french-empire /ledger/12 (vassal_start duchy-of-warsaw, 1807-07). Month from the Treaties of Tilsit (7 and 9 July 1807) and the constitution of 22 July 1807 (see the founding event).
April 1809: with the Austrians invading, the seat moves to Toruń. The infobox lists 'Toruń (de facto, April – May 1809)' beside Warsaw; the page gives no day.

ledger.note: 14 April 1809: Austria invades the duchy. 'invaded the territory of the Duchy of Warsaw on 14 April 1809'; after the stand-off at Raszyn (19 April) 'the Polish forces nonetheless retreated, allowing the Austrians to occupy the duchy's capital, Warsaw'; then 'Polish forces took the major cities of Lublin (14 May), Sandomierz (18 May), Zamość (20 May), and Lwów (27 May)' and Kraków on 15 July.
June 1809: the capital returns to Warsaw. The Austro-Polish War page says the Austrians had to 'abandon Warsaw itself (on 1 June)'; the return of the government is the researcher's reading.

notes:
SCOPE. 1807 (July) to 1815 (9 June), the Congress of Vienna; Cliopatria draws 1809-1813 only, so 1807-1808 and 1814-1815 are new keyframes (the 1809 and 1812 outlines reused). The page gives no formal end date; the 1815 partition is the infobox's Congress of Vienna entry. The Duchy page says 'the existence of the duchy in anything but name came to an end' after January 1813: the occupation events carry that.

CLIOPATRIA DEFECTS. (1) The 1809 shape (100,411 km2) is the pre-Schönbrunn duchy and Cliopatria holds it through 1810; the Treaty of Schönbrunn (14 October 1809) enlarged the duchy, so 1810 uses the 1811 outline. (2) Cliopatria's Kingdom of Prussia has no shape for 1809-1813 (see the Confederation of the Rhine dossier: that row's shapes are the Prussian rump), so the 1807 cession from Prussia cannot be matched.

NOT SETTLED. The Białystok district went to Russia at Tilsit (page: 'became part of Russia'), not to the duchy; Danzig became a Free City, not part of the duchy; the extents of the Grand Duchy of Posen and the Free City of Kraków in 1815 are the researcher's readings. Pages not opened for want of budget: Treaty of Schönbrunn, Treaties of Tilsit, French invasion of Russia.
